correspondences.rationale: Both denote failure of a transmitting optical laser that removes its channel at the remote receiver.
Both denote a whole-card failure that removes traffic and monitoring and may mask subordinate alarms.
Both denote degradation confined to one receiver while the shared optical path and other channels remain normal.
Both denote a physical fibre discontinuity that prevents channel light from propagating.
Both denote complete amplifier failure, from pump or unit failure, producing no optical output and losing all carried channels.
Both denote an unplugged optical patch lead that opens the optical path.
Both denote a ROADM ingress or add port blocking an intended optical channel.
Both denote increased fibre attenuation that reduces received power and margin.
Both denote increased EDFA noise that lowers OSNR without necessarily reducing output power.
Both denote increased differential group delay causing PMD impairment.
Both denote spectral misalignment of a WSS passband that degrades quality while power may remain normal.
Both denote a rapid polarization transition exceeding receiver tracking capability.
Both denote connector contamination that adds loss or reflection and degrades the signal.
Both are generic placeholders for an unspecified underlying failure.
Both denote insufficient amplifier gain causing low output and reduced OSNR across carried channels.
Both denote progressive pump deterioration requiring increasing drive current and culminating in an end-of-life threshold.
Both denote wavelength-dependent amplifier gain imbalance, especially affecting band-edge channels.
Both identify the immediately upstream amplifier as failed and emitting no light.
Both denote OTN switch-fabric failure interrupting traversing ODUs and propagating AIS.
Both denote an erroneous ODU cross-connect to the wrong destination without an optical symptom.
Both denote failure of a client port or its optic that takes down the associated service.
Both denote gradual WSS attenuation drift causing low power after the node.
Both denote failure of one WSS ingress port, blocking its degree while other degrees remain unaffected.
Both denote assertion of the digital loss-of-signal defect.
Both denote inability to acquire or maintain OTU frame alignment.

Both denote suppression of traffic alarms by a dominant equipment alarm.
